definition: AutoGen is Microsoft’s framework for building multi-agent AI applications in which agents chat, use tools and work together.
details: Created by Microsoft Research (Chi Wang, Qingyun Wu and colleagues) in 2023; version 0.4 rebuilt it around an asynchronous, event-driven core. Microsoft has since folded it into the Microsoft Agent Framework.

explainer.lead: How to install AutoGen, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.

quickstart.python:
import asyncio
from autogen_agentchat.agents import AssistantAgent
from autogen_ext.models.openai import OpenAIChatCompletionClient

async def main():
    agent = AssistantAgent("helper", model_client=OpenAIChatCompletionClient(model="gpt-4o-mini"))
    result = await agent.run(task="Name two uses of embeddings.")
    print(result.messages[-1].content)

asyncio.run(main())

explainer.inAi: Prototype teams of agents (planner, coder, critic) that solve a task by conversation.
explainer.jsNote: No official JavaScript package; AutoGen supports Python and .NET.

tiers.eli5: It is a toolkit for setting up several AI helpers that talk to each other and share the work.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers define agents with roles that exchange messages and call tools to complete a task. A pitfall is that more agents mean more coordination overhead and harder debugging; note version 0.4 rebuilt it around an asynchronous, event-driven core and Microsoft has since folded it into the Microsoft Agent Framework.
tiers.paperLevel: A framework created by Microsoft Research in 2023; agents converse in message-passing patterns to solve tasks. Its limits are those of multi-agent coordination, and the project has been superseded into the Microsoft Agent Framework.

explainer.example: A coder agent and a reviewer agent exchange messages, with the reviewer requesting fixes until the code passes.
